title: NFL Week 4 Recap: Key Takeaways, Burning Questions & Fantasy Insights from Sunday’s Games
body:
The NFL’s fourth week of the 2026 season delivered a mix of surprise upsets, emerging storylines and lingering questions that will shape the playoff picture long before the regular season ends. From a hard‑fought victory for the Indianapolis Colts in London to a dramatic showdown between the San Francisco 49ers and the Dallas Cowboys, Sunday’s slate reminded fans that every game now carries weight in an increasingly competitive league. While a handful of teams cemented their early‑season trajectories, several key performances and strategic adjustments left analysts scrambling for answers and fantasy owners recalibrating their line‑ups.

The overseas opener set the tone for the week. The Colts, after a sluggish first half against the Washington Commanders, rallied behind quarterback Anthony Richardson’s poise and a revitalized ground game anchored by Jonathan Taylor. Richardson, who threw for 285 yards and two touchdowns while adding a 42‑yard scramble, erased a 10‑point deficit and capped the comeback with a 12‑yard touchdown pass to Michael Pittman Jr. in the final minutes. Washington’s defense, which had looked dominant in the opening quarter, faltered under the Colts’ balanced attack, allowing 22 points after halftime. The win not only gives Indianapolis its second victory of the season but also marks the first time a rookie quarterback has engineered a comeback win on foreign soil, a milestone that could boost the franchise’s confidence heading into a demanding schedule.

Back on American soil, the NFC East saw the Dallas Cowboys stumble in a tightly contested loss to the 49ers, a game that highlighted the growing pains of a Dallas squad still searching for identity under new head coach Dan Quinn. Despite a strong start from Dak Prescott, who posted 312 passing yards and a touchdown, the Cowboys were unable to contain San Francisco’s versatile offense. The 49ers, led by veteran quarterback Brock Purdy, mixed power‑run concepts with play‑action passes, amassing 375 total yards and three scores. Defensive coordinator DeMeco Ryans’ aggressive blitz package forced three turnovers, including a game‑changing strip‑sack on Prescott in the fourth quarter. The defeat raises questions about Dallas’s ability to protect the ball and adapt to high‑press defenses, especially as the Cowboys look to solidify a playoff berth in a tightly packed NFC East.

In the AFC, the Buffalo Bills continued their dominant start, cruising past the Jacksonville Jaguars 31‑10. Quarterback Josh Allen once again demonstrated why he’s a perennial MVP candidate, delivering 340 yards through the air, two touchdowns and a rushing score. The Bills’ offensive line, now fully healthy after early‑season injuries, gave Allen ample time to exploit Jacksonville’s porous secondary, while the defense forced three sacks and limited the Jaguars to a single field goal after halftime. Jacksonville, meanwhile, struggled to establish a running rhythm, managing just 68 rushing yards, a stark contrast to the ground game they showcased late last season. The loss deepens the Jaguars’ early‑season woes and places them in a precarious position in the AFC South, where every conference game now feels like a must‑win.

The week also featured a surprise resurgence from the New York Giants, who edged out the Los Angeles Rams 24‑21 in a game that hinged on special‑teams play. Giants kicker Graham Gano’s 58‑yard field goal in the closing seconds secured the win, while the Rams’ defense, plagued by missed assignments, allowed a late‑game drive that culminated in a short touchdown pass to Darius Slayton. The victory injects much‑needed momentum into a Giants roster that has struggled with consistency, and it underscores the growing importance of reliable special‑teams units in close contests.

Fantasy managers are already feeling the ripple effects. Richardson’s breakout performance catapults him into the top‑10 quarterback pool, while Prescott’s turnover‑laden outing may prompt owners to seek more stable options. Meanwhile, Brock Purdy’s steady production continues to make him a weekly starter, and Josh Allen’s dual‑threat capability reaffirms his elite status. As injuries remain a variable, depth charts will be closely monitored ahead of the next round of games.

Looking ahead, Week 5 promises to test the resilience of several teams that stumbled this weekend. The Cowboys will travel to face the Seattle Seahawks, a matchup that could either expose Dallas’s defensive deficiencies or force a rapid tactical adjustment. Indianapolis returns home to host the Miami Dolphins, offering Richardson a chance to solidify his status as a rising star before the season’s midpoint. For the Bills and Giants, the next slate presents opportunities to extend their early leads in the AFC East and NFC East, respectively.
